c.v: Merged from the TRM Glossary and the chip Datasheet Glossary.
The Source column gives the document: TRM (Technical Reference Manual) or Datasheet (ESP32-S3 Series Datasheet).
Terms defined in both documents appear on consecutive rows.
The TRM groups its entries as Abbreviations for Peripherals, Abbreviations Related to Registers, and Access Types for Registers; access types are marked "(access type)" below.
The Register Summary and Register Description sections in TRM chapters specify access types for registers and their fields.

Most frequently used access types and their combinations are: R/WS/SS/SC, R/SS/WTC, R/SC/WTC, R/SS/SC/WTC, RF/WF, R/SS/RC, varies, RO, WO, WT, R/W, R/W1, WL, R/W/SC, R/W/SS, R/W/SS/SC, R/WC/SS, R/WC/SC, R/WC/SS/SC, R/WS/SC, R/WS/SS.

A one-time programmable (OTP) memory which stores system and user parameters, such as MAC address, chip revision number, flash encryption key, etc. Value 0 indicates the default state, and value 1 indicates the eFuse has been programmed. (Datasheet p. 39)

A parameter stored in an electrically programmable fuse (eFuse) memory within a chip. The parameter can be set by programming EFUSE_PGM_DATA_n_REG registers, and read by reading a register field named after the parameter. (Datasheet p. 32)
Hardware Read Only. Only hardware can read from this register/field; used for storing default settings for variable parameters.
Flash integrated directly into the chip's package, and external to the chip die. (Datasheet pp. 4, 13)

Isolation. If a peripheral or other chip component is powered down, the pins, if any, to which its output signals are routed will go into a floating state. ISO registers isolate such pins and keep them at a certain determined value, so that the other non-powered-down peripherals/devices attached to these pins are not affected.
A boot mode in which users can download code into flash via the
- Note), and load and execute the downloaded code from the flash or SRAM. (Datasheet p. 33)
A self-contained unit integrated within the chip to extend its capabilities, such as cryptographic modules, RF modules. (Datasheet p. 2)
Non-maskable interrupt is a hardware interrupt that cannot be disabled or ignored by the CPU instructions. Such interrupts exist to signal the occurrence of a critical error.
Flash external to the chip's package. (Datasheet p. 20)
A hardware component or subsystem within the chip to interface with the outside world. (Datasheet p. 2)
Read. User application can read from this register/field; usually combined with other access types.
Read to clear. If user application reads from this register/field, hardware automatically writes 0 to it.
Read from FIFO. If user application writes new data to FIFO, the register/field automatically reads it.
Read only. User application can only read from this register/field.
Read to set. If user application reads from this register/field, hardware automatically writes 1 to it.
Self clear. On a specified event, hardware automatically writes 0 to this register/field; used with
Self modify. On a specified event, hardware automatically writes a specified value to this register/field; used with multi-bit fields.
A boot mode in which users load and execute the existing code from SPI flash. (Datasheet p. 33)
Self set. On a specified event, hardware automatically writes 1 to this register/field; used with
A type of GPIO pin used to configure certain operational settings during the chip's power-up, and can be reconfigured as normal GPIO after the chip's reset. (Datasheet p. 32)
Self update. On a specified event, hardware automatically updates this register/field; used with multi-bit fields.
System registers are a group of registers that control system reset, memory, clocks, software interrupts, power management, clock gating, etc.
The access type varies. Different fields of this register might have different access types.
Write. User application can write to this register/field; usually combined with other access types.
Write 0 to clear. If user application writes 0 to this register/field, hardware automatically clears this register/field.
Write 0 to set. If user application writes 0 to this register/field, hardware automatically sets this register/field.
Write 0 to toggle. If user application writes 0 to this field, hardware automatically inverts the corresponding field; otherwise - no effect.
Write Once. User application can write to this register/field only once; only allowed to write 1; writing 0 is invalid.
Write 1 to clear. If user application writes 1 to this register/field, hardware automatically clears this register/field.
Write 1 to set. If user application writes 1 to this register/field, hardware automatically sets this register/field.
Write 1 to toggle. If user application writes 1 to this field, hardware automatically inverts the corresponding field; otherwise - no effect.

Write any value to clear. If user application writes to this register/field, hardware automatically clears this register/field.
Write to FIFO. If user application writes new data to this register/field, it automatically passes the data to FIFO via APB bus.
Write if a lock is deactivated. If the lock is deactivated, user application can write to this register/field.
Write only. User application can only write to this register/field.
Write any value to set. If user application writes to this register/field, hardware automatically sets this register/field.
Write 1 to trigger an event. If user application writes 1 to this field, this action triggers an event (pulse in the APB bus) or clears a corresponding WTC field (see WTC).
Write to clear. Hardware automatically clears this field if user application writes 1 to the corresponding WT field (see WT).
